verses.zh: 以色列人出埃及地后四百八十年，所罗门作以色列王第四年西弗月，就是二月，开工建造耶和华的殿。
verses.en: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites left Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, during the month Ziv[NOTE:1] (the second month),[NOTE:2] he began building the Lord’s temple.
notes: During the month Ziv. This would be April-May, 966 b.c. by modern reckoning.
Heb “60 cubits.” A cubit was a unit of measure roughly equivalent to 18 inches or 45 cm. Measurements in vv. 2-10 have been converted to feet in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 所罗门王为耶和华所建的殿，长六十肘，宽二十肘，高三十肘。
verses.en: The temple King Solomon built for the Lord was 90 feet[NOTE:1] long, 30 feet[NOTE:2] wide, and 45 feet[NOTE:3] high.
notes: Heb “20 [cubits].”
Heb “30 cubits.”
Heb “20 cubits.”

verses.zh: 殿前的廊子长二十肘，与殿的宽窄一样，阔十肘；
verses.en: The porch in front of the main hall of the temple was 30 feet[NOTE:1] long, corresponding to the width of the temple. It was 15 feet[NOTE:2] wide, extending out from the front of the temple.
notes: Heb “10 cubits.”
Heb “and he built on the wall of the temple an extension all around, the walls of the temple all around, for the main hall and for the holy place, and he made side rooms all around.”

verses.zh: 又为殿做了严紧的窗棂。
verses.en: He made framed windows for the temple.

verses.zh: 靠着殿墙，围着外殿内殿，造了三层旁屋；
verses.en: He built an extension all around the walls of the temple’s main hall and Holy Place and constructed side rooms in it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “five cubits.”

verses.zh: 下层宽五肘，中层宽六肘，上层宽七肘。殿外旁屋的梁木搁在殿墙坎上，免得插入殿墙。
verses.en: The bottom floor of the extension was 7½ feet[NOTE:1] wide, the middle floor 9 feet[NOTE:2] wide, and the third floor 10½ feet[NOTE:3] wide. He made ledges[NOTE:4] on the temple’s outer walls so the beams would not have to be inserted into the walls.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “six cubits.”
Heb “7 cubits.”
Or “offsets” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV); NIV “offset ledges.”
Heb “so that [the beams] would not have a hold in the walls of the temple.”
Heb “finished stone of the quarry,” i.e., stones chiseled and shaped at the time they were taken out of the quarry.

verses.zh: 建殿是用山中凿成的石头。建殿的时候，锤子、斧子，和别样铁器的响声都没有听见。
verses.en: As the temple was being built, only stones shaped at the quarry[NOTE:1] were used; the sound of hammers, pickaxes, or any other iron tool was not heard at the temple while it was being built.
notes: The Hebrew text has “middle,” but the remainder of the verse suggests this is an error.

verses.zh: 在殿右边当中的旁屋有门，门内有旋螺的楼梯，可以上到第二层，从第二层可以上到第三层。
verses.en: The entrance to the bottom[NOTE:1] level of side rooms was on the south side of the temple; stairs went up[NOTE:2] to the middle floor and then on up to the third[NOTE:3] floor.
notes: Heb “by stairs they went up.” The word translated “stairs” occurs only here. Other options are “trapdoors” or “ladders.”
The translation reads with a few medieval Hebrew mss, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate הַשְּׁלִשִׁית (hashelishit, “the third”) rather than MT הַשְּׁלִשִׁים (hashelishim, “the thirty”).
Heb “ built the house and completed it.”

verses.zh: 所罗门建殿，安置香柏木的栋梁，又用香柏木板遮盖。
verses.en: He finished building the temple[NOTE:1] and covered it[NOTE:2] with rafters[NOTE:3] and boards made of cedar.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the house.”
The word occurs only here; the precise meaning is uncertain.
Heb “and rows with cedar wood.”
Heb “5 cubits.” This must refer to the height of each floor or room.

verses.zh: 靠着殿所造的旁屋，每层高五肘，香柏木的栋梁搁在殿墙坎上。
verses.en: He built an extension all around the temple; it was 7½ feet high[NOTE:1] and it was attached to the temple by cedar beams.
notes: The LXX lacks vv. 11-14.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到所罗门说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord’s message came to Solomon:
notes: Heb “walk in.”

verses.zh: 「论到你所建的这殿，你若遵行我的律例，谨守我的典章，遵从我的一切诫命，我必向你应验我所应许你父亲大卫的话。
verses.en: “As for this temple you are building, if you follow[NOTE:1] my rules, observe[NOTE:2] my regulations, and obey all my commandments,[NOTE:3] I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “do.”
Heb “and keep all my commandments by walking in them.”
Heb “I will establish my word with you which I spoke to David your father.”
Heb “ built the house and completed it.”

verses.zh: 我必住在以色列人中间，并不丢弃我民以色列。」
verses.en: I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel.”

verses.zh: 所罗门建造殿宇。
verses.en: So Solomon finished building the temple.[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT reads קִירוֹת (qirot, “walls”), but this should be emended to קוֹרוֹת (qorot, “rafters”). See BDB 900 s.v. קוֹרָה.

verses.zh: 殿里面用香柏木板贴墙，从地到棚顶都用木板遮蔽，又用松木板铺地。
verses.en: He constructed the walls inside the temple with cedar planks; he paneled the inside with wood from the floor of the temple to the rafters[NOTE:1] of the ceiling. He covered the temple floor with boards made from the wood of evergreens.
notes: Heb “He built 20 cubits from the rear areas of the temple with cedar planks from the floor to the walls, and he built it on the inside for an inner sanctuary, for a holy place of holy places.”

verses.zh: 内殿，就是至圣所，长二十肘，从地到棚顶用香柏木板遮蔽（或译：隔断）。
verses.en: He built a wall 30 feet in from the rear of the temple as a partition for an inner sanctuary that would be the Most Holy Place.[NOTE:1] He paneled the wall with cedar planks from the floor to the rafters.[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT reads קִירוֹת (qirot, “walls”), but this should be emended to קוֹרוֹת (qorot, “rafters”). See BDB 900 s.v. קוֹרָה.
Heb “and the house was 40 cubits, that is, the main hall before it.”

verses.zh: 内殿前的外殿，长四十肘。
verses.en: The main hall in front of the inner sanctuary was 60 feet long.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Cedar was inside the temple, carvings of gourds (i.e., gourd-shaped ornaments) and opened flowers; the whole was cedar, no stone was seen.”

verses.zh: 殿里一点石头都不显露，一概用香柏木遮蔽；上面刻着野瓜和初开的花。
verses.en: The inside of the temple was all cedar and was adorned with carvings of round ornaments and of flowers in bloom. Everything was cedar; no stones were visible.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “20 cubits” (this measurement occurs three times in this verse).

verses.zh: 殿里预备了内殿，好安放耶和华的约柜。
verses.en: He prepared the inner sanctuary inside the temple so that the ark of the covenant of the Lord could be placed there.

verses.zh: 内殿长二十肘，宽二十肘，高二十肘，墙面都贴上精金；又用香柏木做坛，包上精金。
verses.en: The inner sanctuary was 30 feet[NOTE:1] long, 30 feet wide, and 30 feet high. He plated it with gold,[NOTE:2] as well as the cedar altar.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “with plated gold” (or perhaps, “with pure gold”).
Heb “he plated [the] altar of cedar.”
Heb “with plated gold” (or perhaps, “with pure gold”).

verses.zh: 所罗门用精金贴了殿内的墙，又用金链子挂在内殿前门扇，用金包裹。
verses.en: Solomon plated the inside of the temple with gold.[NOTE:1] He hung golden chains in front of the inner sanctuary and plated the inner sanctuary[NOTE:2] with gold.
notes: Heb “it.”
Heb “all the temple he plated with gold until all the temple was finished; and the whole altar which was in the inner sanctuary he plated with gold.”

verses.zh: 全殿都贴上金子，直到贴完；内殿前的坛，也都用金包裹。
verses.en: He plated the entire inside of the temple with gold, as well as the altar inside the inner sanctuary.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “10 cubits” (a cubit was a unit of measure roughly equivalent to 18 inches or 45 cm).

verses.zh: 他用橄榄木做两个基路伯，各高十肘，安在内殿。
verses.en: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood; each stood 15 feet[NOTE:1] high.
notes: Heb “The first wing of the [one] cherub was 5 cubits, and the second wing of the cherub was 5 cubits, 10 cubits from the tips of his wings to the tips of his wings.”

verses.zh: 这一个基路伯有两个翅膀，各长五肘，从这翅膀尖到那翅膀尖共有十肘；
verses.en: Each of the first cherub’s wings was 7½ feet long; its entire wingspan was 15 feet.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the second cherub was 10 cubits, the two cherubim had one measurement and one shape.”

verses.zh: 那一个基路伯的两个翅膀也是十肘，两个基路伯的尺寸、形像都是一样。
verses.en: The second cherub also had a wingspan of 15 feet; it was identical to the first in measurements and shape.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the height of the first cherub was 10 cubits; and so was the second cherub.”

verses.zh: 这基路伯高十肘，那基路伯也是如此。
verses.en: Each cherub stood 15 feet high.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in the midst of the inner house,” i.e., in the inner sanctuary.

verses.zh: 他将两个基路伯安在内殿里；基路伯的翅膀是张开的，这基路伯的一个翅膀挨着这边的墙，那基路伯的一个翅膀挨着那边的墙，里边的两个翅膀在殿中间彼此相接；
verses.en: He put the cherubim in the inner sanctuary of the temple.[NOTE:1] Their wings were spread out. One of the first cherub’s wings touched one wall and one of the other cherub’s wings touched the opposite wall. The first cherub’s other wing touched the second cherub’s other wing in the middle of the room.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and their wings were in the middle of the room, touching wing to wing.”
Inside and out probably refers to the inner and outer rooms within the building.

verses.zh: 又用金子包裹二基路伯。
verses.en: He plated the cherubim with gold.

verses.zh: 内殿、外殿周围的墙上都刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花。
verses.en: On all the walls around the temple, inside and out,[NOTE:1] he carved[NOTE:2] cherubim, palm trees, and flowers in bloom.
notes: Heb “carved engravings of carvings.”
Inside and out probably refers to the inner and outer rooms within the building.

verses.zh: 内殿、外殿的地板都贴上金子。
verses.en: He plated the floor of the temple with gold, inside and out.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the pillar, doorposts, a fifth part” (the precise meaning of this description is uncertain).

verses.zh: 又用橄榄木制造内殿的门扇、门楣、门框；门口有墙的五分之一。
verses.en: He made doors of olive wood at the entrance to the inner sanctuary; the pillar on each doorpost was five sided.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “carved carvings of.”

verses.zh: 在橄榄木做的两门扇上刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花，都贴上金子。
verses.en: On the two doors made of olive wood he carved[NOTE:1] cherubim, palm trees, and flowers in bloom, and he plated them with gold.[NOTE:2] He plated the cherubim and the palm trees with hammered gold.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he plated [with] gold” (the precise object is not stated).
Heb “and he hammered out the gold on the cherubim and the palm trees.”
Heb “and so he did at the entrance of the main hall, doorposts of olive wood, from a fourth.”

verses.zh: 又用橄榄木制造外殿的门框，门口有墙的四分之一。
verses.en: In the same way he made doorposts of olive wood for the entrance to the main hall, only with four-sided pillars.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “he also made” are added for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 用松木做门两扇。这扇分两扇，是摺叠的；那扇分两扇，也是摺叠的。
verses.en: He also made[NOTE:1] two doors out of wood from evergreens; each door had two folding leaves.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “two of the leaves of the first door were folding, and two of the leaves of the second door were folding.” In the second half of the description, the MT has קְלָעִים (qelaʿim, “curtains”), but this probably should be emended to צְלָעִים (tselaʿim, “leaves”), which appears in the first half of the statement. One Hebrew ms, the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate support צְלָעִים (tselaʿim, “leaves”).
In the month of Ziv. This would be April-May, 966 b.c. by modern reckoning.

verses.zh: 上面刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花，都用金子贴了。
verses.en: He carved cherubim, palm trees, and flowers in bloom and plated them with gold, leveled out over the carvings.

verses.zh: 他又用凿成的石头三层、香柏木一层建筑内院。
verses.en: He built the inner courtyard with three rows of chiseled stones and a row of cedar beams.

verses.zh: 所罗门在位第四年西弗月，立了耶和华殿的根基。
verses.en: In the month of Ziv[NOTE:1] in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign[NOTE:2] the foundation was laid for the Lord’s temple.
notes: The words “of Solomon’s reign” are added for clarification. See v. 1.
In the month Bul. This would be October-November 959 b.c. in modern reckoning.

verses.zh: 到十一年布勒月，就是八月，殿和一切属殿的都按着样式造成。他建殿的工夫共有七年。
verses.en: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul[NOTE:1] (the eighth month) the temple was completed in accordance with all its specifications and blueprints. It took seven years to build.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he built it in seven years.”
